- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk-off behavior or market recovery.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), especially when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — apply a 1-2 day lag correction.
- In early horizon (e.g., 1-3 days ahead), model often misses short-term volatility; use sentiment to weight recent price momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to recent sentiment swings; apply smoothing or decay factor to sentiment influence (e.g., 70% weight on last 5 days).
- If sentiment is flat or mixed (0.2–0.6), model often fails to capture mean reversion — use 3-5 day average of past 10–15 days as baseline for correction.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes are common in 10–15 day horizon — apply downward bias of 1–3% for each sentiment spike > 0.8.
